participants.note: Concept ACK noting external demand and that libevent's removal enables this
Concept ACK, but reported that a second node can take over a live Unix socket path, leaving the first node unreachable

claims.text: A second node started with the same -rpcbind=unix:<path> will overwrite the live socket file without error, making the first node unreachable while it remains running.
claims.quote: second node can take over a live rpc unix socket path, if two nodes use different datadirs but the same -rpcbind=unix:<path> the second node starts with no error..since it removes the first node socket file and creates its own then after that bitcoin cli talks to the second node.. the first node keeps running but becomes unreachable

support.reason: users of other projects relying on Core have wanted Unix domain socket support, and previous libevent blockers are gone

waiting_on.what: address issue where a second node overwrites an active Unix domain socket path without error
